Recent recipients include Bob Miller, Ed Kashi, Laura Morton, Caitlin O'Hara, Kathy Shorr, Mary Calvert and Nathan Posner. Applications run through Picter and the deadline line reads 4:59pm on 30 November, so treat the afternoon, not midnight, as the cutoff. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $5,000.

item.title: Creators’ Favourite Sluts: A Two-Spirit/Indigiqueer Art Market · grunt gallery
item.description: grunt gallery in Vancouver is bringing back “Creators’ Favourite Sluts”, the Two-Spirit/Indigiqueer art market it first ran in February for Valentine’s Day, for a second edition on Saturday 12 December 2026, and is looking for 2S and/or Queer Indigenous artists from Turtle Island and Palestine to join the roster of tabling artists. It is presented by Vance Wright with the gallery. Applying is not the same as being selected: the intake form says official selections are made at the end of October and that every applicant is told where they stand then, and applications close at 11:59pm on 31 October. The market takes over two rooms of the gallery and there is space for 13 to 15 artists, so most tablers will share a table two to one — you are asked to think honestly about how much table space your work actually needs, and to say in the application if you need more, since the more artists are willing to share the more can be included. grunt provides the tables and chairs; artists handle their own transactions and keep 100% of their proceeds. There is no fee to apply and no fee for the table. The form asks every applicant for three to five images of their work and a bio of up to 100 words, plus pronouns and a short description of what you plan to sell. Neither the call nor the form uses the word photography: what the form asks for is “a short description of the artwork or wares you plan on selling”, offering “beadwork, paintings, prints, stickers, etc.” as its examples, so a photographer with prints or zines applies on the same footing as any other maker. The market runs 1pm to 7pm with load-in from 12:30pm, and grunt says to get in touch if those hours do not work for you. Access information for the space is published at the foot of grunt’s events page, and the gallery invites specific access questions by email. What is on offer is a free table at an artist-run centre that has been in Vancouver since 1984, in front of its audience, with nothing taken off the top. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: 2027 Black Artist Showcase · Jamestown Settlement
item.description: Jamestown Settlement, the living-history museum run by the Jamestown-Yorktown Foundation near the site of England's first permanent North American colony, invites adult Black visual artists living in Virginia to submit work for its 2027 Black Artist Showcase, hung along the Great Hall passageways that lead into the museum's main galleries from 30 January to 28 March 2027. The theme is "Founders and Foundations", and the call is open to any medium — the museum's own listing names painting, drawing, printmaking, graphic arts and photography — which makes this one of the few state-museum exhibition slots a photographer can reach without an entry fee of any kind. Up to three works may be submitted on the museum's own web form, each needing a title, medium, accurate framed dimensions and a reference JPEG or PNG under 5 MB. Selected artists are notified by 16 November 2026 and sign a Memorandum of Agreement with the Foundation, which pays a small honorarium at the close of the showcase; artists must return a signed Virginia substitute W-9 by 30 December 2026 or their work cannot be hung. Work is delivered in person to Jamestown Settlement between 11 and 24 January 2027, by appointment, and must arrive exhibition-ready: works on paper glazed and framed, hanging hardware already installed, D-rings preferred to wire. The Foundation states plainly that it will not prepare, mount, frame or fit hardware to any work, and that anything arriving not exhibit-ready is dropped from the showcase. Two public events sit inside the run: the "After Angelo" daytime celebration of African American heritage on 20 February 2027, where showcase artists may reserve a vendor table and sell their own work, and a "Last Looks" closing reception on the evening of 27 March 2027. Artists collect their work between 3 and 10 April 2027. — Deadline: November 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Museum exhibition + honorarium.

item.title: Call for Curators: The Gallery at the Attucks 2027 · Norfolk Arts
item.description: Norfolk Arts, the City of Norfolk's municipal arts agency, is looking for a curator to build the 2027 exhibition at The Gallery at the Attucks — the gallery inside the Attucks Theatre on Church Street, built in 1919 and described by Norfolk Arts as the oldest remaining Black-owned and Black-built theatre in the United States. The brief asks for a group exhibition of at least seven artists with a connection to Hampton Roads, in contemporary 2-D work only, that speaks to the Attucks' cultural legacy; Norfolk Arts says Black curators are strongly encouraged to apply. Proposals are expected to set out a clear strategy for drawing large and diverse audiences, and partnerships, cross-disciplinary ideas and additional programming — artist talks, performances, demonstrations — are preferred. The money is real and unusually transparent for a municipal call: $1,500 goes to the curator and $3,500 is divided among the exhibiting artists, there is no application fee, and the gallery takes no commission on sales, which artists may choose to allow or not. The show runs for six months in a space of roughly 1,500 square feet. Because this is a city contract, the curator and the participating artists each upload a W-9 and register as a City of Norfolk vendor to be paid. The curator may not exhibit their own work, which makes this a genuine curatorial commission rather than a route to a self-made show — and for photographers, a 2-D-only brief in a six-month municipal gallery slot is one of the few places a Hampton Roads practice can be seen at that length. Materials are emailed to Norfolk Arts by 11:59pm on 8 December 2026; the agency publishes a full prospectus PDF alongside the call. Curators are notified by 8 January 2027 and the first exhibition installs in mid-April 2027. — Deadline: December 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,500 curator stipend + $3,500 artist stipends + 6-month exhibition.

item.title: Art in Transit Open Call for Artwork · WMATA Art in Transit
item.description: Metro's Office of Community Engagement runs a standing, no-fee open call to build a pool of artists whose work can be placed across the Washington transit system — and photography is one of the nine disciplines it names explicitly, not an afterthought. Five formats are on offer. Barricade and construction-wall art turns the temporary barriers around station works into large-scale vinyl wraps or printed panels, so files need to arrive in a modifiable digital format suitable for vinyl, corrugated plastic or aluminium. Digital screen activations put photography, animation and other digital media on screens throughout stations, transit hubs and Metro facilities, with a twenty-second run-time cap and a requirement that the work can be reformatted for custom screen sizes. Station and facility installations are temporary exhibitions in mezzanines, corridors and other public-facing spaces, two- or three-dimensional, on view for up to three years. The remaining two routes cover community and special-event activations — commemorations, cultural celebrations, anniversary programmes — and a catch-all for new spaces and technologies as they appear. Eligibility is regional and clearly stated: artists and creatives resident in the District of Columbia, Maryland and Virginia, aged 18 or over, working individually or in teams, with priority to artists inside Metro's registered service area; emerging, mid-career and established practitioners are all invited, and Metro says artists from historically underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply. The application is one form asking for a 50-word bio, a 100-word statement, five work samples as JPEG or PNG, a portfolio or social link and a CV of no more than two pages. Submissions go to the Art in Transit programme team and stay on file for current and future opportunities; for multi-year temporary projects a Community Advisory Group of Metro staff, local residents and regional public-art specialists may be convened for the final choice. Selection is not guaranteed by applying, but if a project does come, the artist submits a quote and Metro provides a budget covering the artist fee and any file-preparation labour. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Artist fee from a project budget + temporary exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Proposals: Main and Nano Galleries · DC Arts Center
item.description: The DC Arts Center in Adams Morgan takes exhibition proposals and bodies of work from artists and curators year-round, for both of its newly renovated galleries: the Main Gallery, roughly 700 square feet and built for full-size work in any medium, and the Nano Gallery, roughly 125 square feet for small-format work that hangs easily. You can indicate which space suits your work, but DCAC makes the final placement call. What makes this one worth understanding before applying is that DCAC is explicitly curator-driven: an accepted application does not book you a show, it puts you on the centre's roster of approved exhibiting artists, whose materials the curatorial team reviews when planning future exhibitions. From there a curator may pick up an already-curated proposal as submitted, pull one or more pieces from your submitted body of work into a group show, or pair you with a curator from DCAC's roster to shape the proposal together — and if a curator is interested, the next step is a studio visit. DCAC is candid that this stage moves on the gallery's own schedule, quickly or slowly, and that your work stays active in the system either way. Unsuccessful applicants are told so and are sent the committee's feedback, with an invitation to apply again once it has been worked through. The application needs an artist statement and biography, a résumé, proposed exhibition title and description, an image or video list, and high-resolution files that show the work as you intend it to be exhibited. The fee is $25, waived for DCAC Artist Members. Proposals are reviewed quarterly by the Visual Arts Committee, which judges artistic quality, conceptual coherence, readiness for exhibition, growth potential, alignment with DCAC's mission, and marketability. Artists keep 60% of the sale price on work sold, or 70% as Artist Members. DCAC states it supports artists at all stages of their careers and across all disciplines, welcomes applications from all artists, and does not discriminate on any basis. Two restrictions sit alongside that sentence under the page's own Eligibility heading, which it prints twice: “You must be a local artist or curator working in the DMV (DC, Maryland, Virginia)”, and artists who have presented a solo show at DCAC within the past three years cannot have another solo exhibition until three years have passed from its closing date, though they may still be included in a group show. Applicants must also be available to attend an Opening Celebration, an Artist Talk and a Closing Reception in person. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $25 (free for DCAC Artist Members). Prize: Gallery exhibition + 60–70% of sales.

item.title: FeelsZine Issue 28 — Play
item.description: FEELS is a Canadian independent zine that has published two issues a year, in January and July, since Issue 01 in January 2017, and Issue 28 takes "Play" as its theme — the mission statement for it is still being written, which leaves the brief unusually open for anyone submitting early. The zine is deliberately multidisciplinary: photography sits alongside illustration, art, collage, comics and typography, and those run next to poetry, personal essays, fiction and interview proposals. Pitches for something not on that list are explicitly welcomed. Every accepted submission earns a $60 honorarium and a free copy of the issue, which is a real rate for a small independent publication and a meaningful change from the $25 the zine paid for Issue 27. Submission is free and goes by email with a short bio, a description of the work, and a statement of your personal connection to the issue topic — FEELS prioritises stories and art grounded in lived experience. Photographic and art submissions need a short artist statement; the zine is printed at 6.5 × 9.5 inches with a 0.125-inch bleed, low-res proofs are fine to submit, and accepted work is requested at 300dpi for print. Writing is capped at 1,800 words for longform, two poems or less unless part of a single collection of up to four. The editors ask for one or two works per person given submission volume, and promise to reply to every email. Previously published work is accepted so long as it will not appear in another Canadian independent magazine during the same six-month publication window, with attribution included if the original publisher requires it. FEELS publishes a majority of Canadian content as a Canadian publication but does include global contributors, and the call states plainly that it welcomes and encourages people of all diverse experiences, abilities and communities. The zine is also explicit about machine-made work: "We are an anti-AI publication and do not accept any pieces using generative AI." The deadline is 15 March 2027 and the issue is released in July 2027. — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication + $60 honorarium.

item.title: Call for Curatorial & Exhibition Proposals · Art Works Downtown
item.description: Art Works Downtown, the 501(c)(3) non-profit arts organisation whose 40,000-square-foot building at 1325-1337 Fourth Street in downtown San Rafael houses galleries and 33 artist studios, takes proposals on a rolling basis for Gallery 1337, its primary exhibition space. The invitation is deliberately wide: emerging and established curators, independent curators, artists, and collaborative teams may propose solo or group exhibitions, and AWD says it is looking for "projects with a clear vision, strong artistic quality, professionalism, originality, and a compelling concept suited to the gallery and our public audience." What makes this worth a photographer's or curator's time is that AWD budgets for the work the proposal implies rather than simply lending a wall: selected projects may receive up to $5,000 in curatorial or exhibition support, use of Gallery 1337, exhibition planning and production support, advertising and promotion, gallery staffing during public hours (Wednesday to Saturday, 11am to 5pm), two exhibition receptions, and support for related public programs. There is no application fee. A proposal should carry the exhibition title; a curatorial or exhibition statement setting out concept, themes and goals; curator and/or artist bio and CV; participating artists with brief bios and portfolio links if they are already identified; representative artwork images with artist, title, medium, dimensions, date and price where applicable; the proposed number and type of works; an installation concept with any technical or equipment needs; preferred dates and timeline; public programming ideas; audience, outreach or partnership ideas; and a preliminary budget naming the intended use of any requested stipend. Proposals are weighed on strength and originality of concept, quality of artwork, professionalism and completeness, feasibility, appropriate scale and quantity, ability to engage a broad public audience, inclusivity, diversity, equity, accessibility and representation, and the potential for meaningful public programs. Photographic work is squarely inside the artwork guidelines — AWD primarily exhibits original artwork and permits signed and numbered limited editions, while un-editioned reproductions and print-to-order works are generally not accepted; video and new media are welcome, though most equipment must come from the artist or curator, audio normally needs headphones, and projection may be limited by ambient light. Explicit sexual content and graphic violence are not eligible. Artists should generally reside within 100 miles of San Rafael unless otherwise approved. At least half the exhibited work should be available for sale; AWD processes sales and the tax, keeping 40% of the retail price and paying 60% to the artist unless something else is agreed in writing. Proposals go by email to the exhibitions contact, with no phone calls; AWD warns that the volume of submissions means it may not answer every applicant and cannot give individual critiques, and that it will reach out directly where a proposal fits an upcoming slot. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000 + exhibition.

item.title: FUTURES Baltic Talents 2027 · ISSP
item.description: ISSP, the Riga-based photography institution that has been the Baltic member of the FUTURES Photography Platform since 2022, is looking for three artists from Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia to join the platform's 2027 cohort. FUTURES was founded in 2018 with support from the EU's Creative Europe Culture programme and now pools the talent programmes of twenty leading European photography institutions, each nominating new artists every year. Selected artists receive a participation grant of €500; conversations with international professionals, online and in person; an invitation to the FUTURES Annual Event in autumn 2027 with travel and accommodation covered; access to an online learning programme run with Magnum Photos; the chance to apply to the platform's internal open call for the travelling Annual Exhibition; the chance to apply for a funded FUTURES residency and a tutoring session; invitations to events hosted by the platform's other members; and an artist page plus promotion through the FUTURES website, social media and annual publication. Access to the Magnum learning programme, the FUTURES Conversations, the annual exhibition call, the residency call, the artist page and the member invitations all continue in the years that follow. Three conditions have to hold: you are based in or come from Latvia, Lithuania or Estonia — citizenship or official residency status in one of the three countries — you can show dedication and continuity in your practice over at least three years including at least one exhibition, and you can submit a strong photographic work made in the last three years. Artists who applied in previous years are invited to apply again. The application is free: a Google Form with a PDF of one recent project, due at midnight EET on 6 December 2026. The selection committee is ISSP's own programme and managing directors together with an Estonian and a Lithuanian colleague, and it weighs who would benefit most from the platform's exposure, networking and learning. Selected candidates are notified by 20 December and must have a CV, a portrait and fifteen low- and high-resolution images ready by 1 January. — Deadline: December 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500.

item.title: WC Gallery Installation Proposals · New Hampshire Art Association
item.description: The oddest room in the New Hampshire Art Association's Portsmouth gallery is its bathroom, and the association runs it as an exhibition space. In the association's words the WC Gallery is "an irregular installation space" and it is looking for artists "exploring innovative ideas and taking creative risks to create a visually and mentally stimulating experience". Installations run in three intervals a year — February–May, June–August and September–December — and the brief is to keep the bathroom functional while making it immersive and actively engaging for visitors: a mural or wall work, found objects, or any idea that transforms the room. NHAA publishes a photograph and a dimensioned diagram of the space and encourages artists to come and see it in person. Proposals are accepted on a rolling basis and artists may submit more than one. A proposal is a one-page plan with a diagram showing images or drawings of what will go where, the materials involved (paint, hung work, 3D objects), what the artist will need from the gallery (pedestals, labels), a title, preferred months of installation, and a timeline of what is already made and what will be. Open to regional artists, NHAA members and non-members alike, and free to propose. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Versions of Me: The Artist as Subject · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on the artist as subject. The gallery's framing: the self-portrait has long offered artists a means of exploring identity, experimenting with representation and recording their presence in the world, and in photography the artist becomes both observer and observed, making an image that may reveal, conceal, question or reinvent the self. Praxis seeks work ranging from direct studies of the face and body to reflections, shadows, staged encounters, assumed identities, objects, environments and traces of presence — interpretations of self-portraiture that express, suggest or complicate our understanding of the person who made it. Up to 38 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (19 December 2026 – 9 January 2027), featured on the gallery's online exhibition page and permanently archived there. Awards are a Directors' Choice (free entry into two future juried calls of the artist's choice) and five honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery. Entrants must be 18 or older, and images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission from the gallery. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames and retains a 50% commission on any print sales. Notification is 27 November 2026. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: London Showcase · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's London showcase at The Factory, 21–31 Shacklewell Lane, London E8, from 27 to 29 November 2026. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. Physical places start at £150 and digital places at £50. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in".
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup: the application link asks for a first name and email address, says applications are not public, and sends access to the form by email. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: Free (£150+ physical, £50+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Paris Showcase · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's Paris showcase at 18 rue Lally Tollendal, Paris, from 5 to 7 February 2027. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. The Paris listing does not print its prices; HUGE's general terms are from £150 for a physical place and from £50 for a digital one. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in".
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup: the application link asks for a first name and email address, says applications are not public, and sends access to the form by email. — Deadline: January 20, 2027. Fee: Free (£150+ physical, £50+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Lyon Showcase · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's Lyon showcase at 53 Cours Tolstoï in Villeurbanne, on the edge of Lyon, from 4 to 6 December 2026. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. For Lyon, physical places start at £100 and digital places at £45. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in".
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup: the application link asks for a first name and email address, says applications are not public, and sends access to the form by email. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: Free (£100+ physical, £45+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Tokyo 2027 · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's Tokyo showcase at Design Festa Gallery Harajuku WEST, from 5 to 7 March 2027. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. It is open to emerging, independent, self-taught and formally trained artists working in any medium, photography included, and artists do not need to live locally or attend.
Applying is free, but places are paid for by the artists who are selected. For Tokyo, physical places start at £300 and digital places at £80. A physical place includes presentation in the venue, an artist page on HUGE's website for two years, documentation and a social media feature; a digital place covers on-screen and online presentation. HUGE's own pitch is "If it fits, you're in". The Tokyo application form adds that exhibition spaces are limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
Unlike HUGE's European shows, Tokyo applications go straight to a Typeform without a mailing-list step. — Deadline: February 25, 2027. Fee: Free (£300+ physical, £80+ digital if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Contradiction · Sebastopol Center for the Arts
item.description:
A juried exhibition at Sebastopol Center for the Arts built on paradox. The call asks for work that lives in the tension between opposing forces rather than resolving it: "Consider how things that shouldn't belong together insist on being together. Consider an enigma, a paradox. Bitter/sweet, organized chaos, strange bedfellows. What happens when fire meets ice, big meets little, or grief meets joy?" SebArts offers a list of starting points - bitter and sweet, fire and ice, grief and joy, dark and light, sun and moon, logic and imagination, life and death, opposites on the colour wheel - and states that the work "doesn't need to resolve the tension. It needs to inhabit it." The show runs 27 February to 11 April 2027 at the centre's gallery in Sebastopol, with an opening reception on 27 February, 2-4pm.
SebArts invites "artists working in any medium", so photographic work is eligible, and the organisation adds that it welcomes "artists of all backgrounds and perspectives". Awards are $300 for first place, $200 for second, $100 for third, and two $50 coordinator awards. Work sold during the exhibition splits 60% to the artist and 40% to SebArts. Jurors are listed as TBA; jurying runs 7-14 January 2027 and artists are notified by email on 15 January 2027.
Entry is online only, at $35 for a first application and $10 each for a second and third - a maximum of three separate submissions, each entered one at a time, with up to three JPEG images of 5MB or less per entry. Work must not have been shown previously in the SebArts gallery and should have been made in the last five years. Accepted work is delivered at the artist's expense: shipped pieces must arrive by 19 February 2027 with a prepaid return label and a reusable container, or be hand-delivered on 21 or 23 February, and picked up on 12 April. Wall-hung work is capped at 50 lbs and free-standing work at 300 lbs, with a maximum width of 64 inches for a 10-foot wall. Selected work must stay up for the whole run, and anything left 30 days after the close becomes SebArts property. — Deadline: January 6, 2027. Fee: $35 (2 images), $10 each additional. Prize: $300 / $200 / $100 + two $50 coordinator awards + Group exhibition.

item.title: ARC + ATHENA Artist Residency 2027 · ARC Gallery
item.description:
A new ten-month remote residency from A.R.C. Gallery, the artist-run Chicago cooperative founded in 1973, funded by its philanthropic partner ATHENA and administered by the ARC Gallery & Educational Foundation. Three artists are selected each year from an international pool and work as a cohort, developing individual bodies of work while meeting weekly online with each other and monthly with ARC member mentors, alongside professional development sessions on exhibition preparation, documentation, writing, networking and career sustainability, and introductions to visiting curators and arts professionals.
The 2027 cycle runs February to November 2027 and culminates in three concurrent solo exhibitions at ARC Gallery in Chicago in November 2027. Residents work from their own studios - relocation is not required - but should plan to travel to Chicago for installation and the opening, and travel costs are not covered. Each resident receives $1,500 through ATHENA: a $1,200 artist stipend plus a $300 shipping allowance that may instead go toward materials. ARC takes no commission, so 100% of any sale price goes to the artist, and installation, de-installation, press, social media and a first-Friday opening reception are handled by ARC members. The residency includes a community-engagement element - a demonstration or workshop - and the application asks what you would like it to be.
The call is open to artists working in any medium at any education level, with no stated geographic or age bar, though the CV you paste into the form should demonstrate at least four years of serious pursuit of a career in art. The application takes 10 images (JPG/JPEG; video work as a still plus a clip of up to two minutes in MP4/MOV), an artist statement of no more than 125 words, a two-page CV, two professional references and written answers on process, workspace and internet reliability, collaboration, what you hope to explore, and why ARC. Images are uploaded to Dropbox before the form is paid for. Applications close 15 December 2026 at 11:59 pm CST; review is in January and notification in early February 2027. Entry is $40, and ARC states that limited fee waivers are available on request by email before submitting. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $40 (waivers available). Prize: Ten-month residency + solo exhibition + $1,500.

item.title: The Petrides Residency for a Greek Artist in NY · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description:
A fully funded three-month residency in New York for one artist based in Greece, newly established by the Athens- and New York-based sculptor George Petrides with the International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP) in Brooklyn and administered by NYFA. Photography is one of seven named eligible disciplines, alongside craft/sculpture, digital/electronic arts, interdisciplinary work, painting, printmaking/drawing/book arts and video/film.
The inaugural residency runs 1 October to 31 December 2027 at ISCP, 1040 Metropolitan Avenue, Brooklyn. The selected artist receives 24/7 access to a private furnished studio of 334 square feet, a monthly stipend of $3,000 for accommodation, living expenses and materials ($9,000 across the three months), and a one-time payment of $1,000 toward airfare and local travel. The programme includes at least one hour-long meeting a month with visiting critics, field trips, gallery walks and Fall Open Studios, and the option to join NYFA's professional development programmes. The artist arranges their own travel and housing; ISCP expects roughly 20 studio hours a week.
To apply you must be a practising artist in one or more of the eligible disciplines, hold a valid Greek passport, be a current full-time resident of Greece and have been for at least two years at the time applications opened, be 30 or older by 20 October 2026, have working English, and not be enrolled in a full-time degree programme. Artist duos of two may apply together on one shared stipend and studio. Proof of residency and age is required of the selected artist.
The application asks for a CV or bio of up to five pages, up to 10 images (or a mix of 5 images and one audio/video link), a 150-word work-sample note and three 250-word statements on the proposed project, the practice and why New York. An independent three-person panel scores applications, shortlists three finalists for virtual interviews and makes the final choice; all applicants hear in February 2027 and the recipient is announced publicly in March. Applications must be in English and go through Submittable; there is no application fee. — Deadline: December 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $9,000 stipend + Residency.

item.title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants - Cycle 39 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description:
One-time grants of up to $5,000 for recent unexpected medical, dental and mental-health emergencies, funded by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and administered by NYFA. The eligible Visual Arts category names Photography outright - 'work in traditional and experimental photography or any work in which photography or photographic techniques are pivotal, if not exclusive' - alongside craft/sculpture, painting and printmaking/drawing/book arts, and the programme also covers digital/electronic arts, video/film and choreography.
Applicants must be 21 or older, reside in the United States, the District of Columbia, a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory, and meet the income cap: adjusted gross income no greater than $80,000 for an individual or $160,000 for joint filers, averaged over the last two federal tax returns. You also need recent and sustained artistic activity - at least one public-facing opportunity a year since 2022 - and you cannot be enrolled in any degree-seeking programme or have received a Rauschenberg Medical or Dancer Emergency Grant within the last five years.
Cycle 39 covers emergencies occurring on or after 1 April 2026. Applications opened 20 October and close at 5:00 PM ET on 17 November 2026, with notification on 23 December 2026. Treatment is only covered if it took place in the U.S., D.C., a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory. Artists whose direct medical costs are covered by Medicare or Medicaid may instead request up to $5,000 in documented living expenses. Portfolios and work samples are not requested - applications are reviewed for demonstrated need - but your CV must show five years of practice. Roughly $138,000 is distributed each cycle and demand outstrips it, so applying is not a guarantee of an award. Awarding is a two-step process: NYFA staff screen for eligibility, an outside panel then scores on demonstrated need and severity, and after that review the top-scoring application is funded automatically while the rest of the top tier go into a lottery for the remaining awards. Cycle 40 opens 15 December 2026 and closes 12 January 2027. — Deadline: November 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000.
